summary: Flutter TEXT and DM composers expose the mobile keyboard Send action and route its submission through the existing send flow, matching web's Enter-to-send behavior. Shift+Enter remains a newline in TEXT. Automated verification passed; physical Gboard/Samsung acceptance remains open.

checks.name: TEXT soft-keyboard action regression reproduced before implementation
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub test/workspace_screen_test.dart --plain-name 'text composer submits from the soft-keyboard send action'
checks.observation: The test initially failed because the Android TEXT composer did not expose TextInputAction.send.

checks.name: TEXT and DM soft-keyboard send regressions
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub test/workspace_screen_test.dart --plain-name 'composer submits from the soft-keyboard'
checks.observation: Both TEXT and DM expose TextInputAction.send and submit the entered message when the platform sends that action.

checks.name: Full Flutter suite and analyzer
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub && flutter analyze --no-pub
checks.observation: All 291 Flutter tests pass and flutter analyze reports no issues.

checks.name: Android debug APK build
checks.observation: Android debug APK builds successfully. Flutter reported existing Kotlin Gradle Plugin migration warnings for flutter_background, flutter_webrtc and livekit_client.

checks.name: Physical Android Gboard/Samsung acceptance
checks.observation: Widget tests exercise the platform TextInputAction callback but do not verify actual Gboard rendering, IME behavior, or device-specific submission.

remaining: Install a build containing this change on Samsung/Gboard and verify Send is visible and submits once in TEXT and DM; verify normal multiline/Shift+Enter behavior is unchanged. Keep this physical check under QA-13.
